title: The Bright Protocol
premise: Dominic Underhill, the seventh clone of a murdered beacon engineer, keeps the Bright Protocol running on a dying colony world — a signal loop nobody commissioned and no one can decode. When the colony's children begin sharing one identical dream, the dream turns out to be the beacon's true message: a record proving Earth's government engineered the war that stranded the colonists, delivered in fragments only young minds can receive. As Earth's last transmission loop nears its end, Dominic must choose between broadcasting the truth — which will ignite open rebellion and doom any hope of rescue — or suppressing it and preserving the fragile lie that keeps the colony alive. He broadcasts it, and in the final chapter the children's dream changes: not to war, but to a map home, revealing the beacon's original architect was the first Dominic, who built the message to force humanity to stop running from its own crime.
about_author: Rafael Montrose is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent a decade calibrating deep-space arrays before turning to fiction. He writes about signals, memory, and the people who keep the lights on at the edge of the dark.

chapters.title: The Loop That Outlived Its Maker
chapters.summary: Dominic Underhill performs his daily maintenance on the beacon tower, logging anomalies in a signal no one remembers commissioning. His POV establishes his routine, his inherited memories of the original's murder, and his loneliness. Emotional beat: quiet duty shadowed by the question of who he was before he was himself.

chapters.title: Seventh of His Name
chapters.summary: Dominic reviews the clone registry and the unsolved murder file he inherited. Flashbacks through borrowed memories show the original Dominic's final hours. He visits his own predecessor's grave. Emotional beat: grief for a man whose death he remembers but never lived.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Night
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Mara Voss, POV, notices her students drawing the same impossible structure — a tower of light none of them have seen. She brings the drawings to the council, who dismiss her. Emotional beat: creeping unease beneath the colony's brittle normalcy.

chapters.title: The Council of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Councilor Ade Rask, POV, reveals to the reader that the colony's food synthesizers are failing and Earth's resupply is a decade late. He quietly orders information suppressed to prevent panic. Emotional beat: the corrosion of good intentions.

chapters.title: A Dream in Common
chapters.summary: Dominic is summoned to the school after a child describes the beacon's interior — a place sealed since before her birth. He recognizes details only he should know. Emotional beat: the first crack in his belief that his secrets are his own.

chapters.title: Static That Answers
chapters.summary: Dominic runs diagnostics and finds the beacon's signal has changed: it now modulates in rhythm with the children's sleep cycles. Someone or something is using it as a transmitter. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Murder File, Reopened
chapters.summary: Dominic rereads the original's notes and finds a hidden addendum: the beacon was built to carry a message the original died protecting. POV alternates with the dead man's journal entries. Emotional beat: the past pressing its hand against the present.

chapters.title: What the Children Saw
chapters.summary: Mara gathers testimony from eleven dreaming children; their accounts interlock into a coherent image — a war room, a decision, a betrayal. Emotional beat: the horror of innocence used as a vessel.

chapters.title: Rask's Quiet Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ade Rask calculates how many colonists the failing synthesizers can sustain and begins a covert triage list. POV Rask. Emotional beat: power assumed in the dark, justified as mercy.

chapters.title: The Man Who Came Back
chapters.summary: A shuttle arrives carrying Earth envoy Ilse Marchetti, the first contact in nine years — and she demands the beacon be shut down. Emotional beat: hope arriving wearing the face of a threat.

chapters.title: Shutdown Order
chapters.summary: Marchetti presents evidence the beacon is jamming Earth's military channels and that its continued operation constitutes treason. Rask, seeing leverage, supports her. Emotional beat: the colony's survival bartered away in a single meeting.

chapters.title: Night Shift at the End of the World
chapters.summary: Dominic defies the shutdown, hiding the beacon's core behind a maintenance loop. He confesses his clone status to Mara, trusting her with the one thing that could destroy him. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared danger.

chapters.title: The Dream Deepens
chapters.summary: The children's shared dream advances: they now witness the moment the original Dominic hid the message inside the signal. Mara realizes the dream is a playback, not a haunting. Emotional beat: revelation as vertigo.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Marchetti reveals privately to Rask that Earth is losing the war and this transmission loop is its final broadcast window — after which the colony is officially written off. Emotional beat: abandonment dressed as procedure.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone destroys the beacon's backup power array. Dominic suspects Marchetti's security detail; the evidence points instead to someone inside the colony. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: The Grave Digger's Confession
chapters.summary: An old technician, dying, admits to Mara that he helped bury the original's findings years ago under council orders — the colony's founders knew what the beacon carried. Emotional beat: complicity across generations.

chapters.title: Decoding the Dream
chapters.summary: Dominic and Mara cross-reference the children's dream imagery with the original's cipher notes and recover the first fragment: a date, a name, and the word 'ordered.' Emotional beat: the thrill of the lock turning.

chapters.title: Rask's List
chapters.summary: Mara discovers Rask's triage list and realizes the council has already decided who will starve. She faces the choice of exposure versus collapse. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — the truth she carries could kill faster than the lie.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Marchetti detains Dominic, probing his clone memories for the beacon's access keys. Under pressure he realizes she already knows what the message contains. Emotional beat: the hunted realizing he was never the prey.

chapters.title: The Original's Vault
chapters.summary: Following a dream fragment only he can interpret — because the memories are his — Dominic finds the original's hidden vault beneath the tower: recordings proving Earth's high command engineered the colony's abandonment to cover a war crime. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Two Dominics
chapters.summary: In the vault, Dominic watches his original's final message, addressed to 'whoever I become.' It asks him to finish the work, and forgives him in advance for whatever it costs. Emotional beat: the most intimate scene — a man receiving permission from himself.

chapters.title: Coup at Dawn
chapters.summary: Rask, learning of the vault, seizes the tower with council security, declaring emergency authority. Marchetti's marines stand by, letting the colonists disarm each other. Emotional beat: the war arriving not from Earth but from within.

chapters.title: The Children Stop Dreaming
chapters.summary: The shared dream cuts off mid-message when Rask powers down the beacon. The children wake screaming, and the colony's fear tips toward riot. Emotional beat: silence as violence.

chapters.title: Mara's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara trades the vault's location to Marchetti in exchange for the children's safety, betraying Dominic to save her students. Emotional beat: betrayal as an act of love.

chapters.title: The Loop's Last Hours
chapters.summary: Dominic, imprisoned in the tower's lower levels, learns from a sympathetic guard that Earth's transmission window closes in thirty-six hours. After that, the message can never reach anyone. Emotional beat: a clock starting in the dark.

chapters.title: Rask's Confession
chapters.summary: Rask visits Dominic and reveals the triage list was modeled on Earth's own abandonment protocols — he learned ruthlessness from the people he's protecting the colony from. Emotional beat: the villain made legible, not forgiven.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Signal
chapters.summary: Dominic uses the beacon's own resonance — the frequency the children dreamed — to overload the tower's locks and escape into the storm season. Emotional beat: the message itself becoming a weapon for its bearer.

chapters.title: The Long Walk
chapters.summary: Dominic crosses the frozen wastes toward the colony's old comm array, pursued by marines. POV alternates with Mara stalling Marchetti. Emotional beat: endurance stripped to its essentials.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: The children, dreaming again now that the beacon flickers back to life, begin reciting the message's final coordinates aloud in unison. Marchetti realizes suppressing it has become impossible. Emotional beat: the truth escaping through the mouths of the young.

chapters.title: Storm Front
chapters.summary: Dominic reaches the comm array as a hurricane-force storm hits; the marines' shuttle crashes, forcing him to save the same soldiers hunting him. Emotional beat: mercy offered to an enemy at the edge of survival.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: At the array, Dominic faces the final decision: broadcast the message and shatter the colony's last hope of Earth's rescue, or stay silent and let the crime stay buried. He remembers the original's forgiveness. Emotional beat: the fulcrum of the book.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dominic transmits the full message — Earth's war crime, the abandonment order, the original's testimony — into Earth's last open loop. Across the colony, every screen and speaker carries it. Emotional beat: catharsis and dread in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Colony Answers
chapters.summary: Instead of riot, the colonists go silent, then begin lighting every lamp and beacon they own — a signal of acknowledgment, not rebellion. Rask resigns publicly. Emotional beat: a community choosing truth over comfort.

chapters.title: Marchetti's Report
chapters.summary: POV Marchetti: she files her official report, then a second, sealed one — her own admission of what she was ordered to bury. She chooses, finally, not to fire on the tower. Emotional beat: an instrument of power defecting to the truth.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Weeks pass. Earth's response is a single transmission: coordinates. The war has ended, and the colony — the crime's living witnesses — is named as the terms of the peace. Emotional beat: stunned, cautious hope.

chapters.title: The Dream Changes
chapters.summary: The children dream one last time: not the war room, but a route home — the original Dominic's final gift, a navigation solution hidden in the message's coda. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Tower
chapters.summary: Dominic and Mara repair the beacon together, no longer as a warning but as a lighthouse for the ships to come. Rask, demoted, volunteers for the work crews. Emotional beat: atonement through labor.

chapters.title: The Grave, Revisited
chapters.summary: Dominic visits the original's grave and finally speaks to him as himself — not a copy, but a continuation. He buries the murder file, the case closed at last. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: First Light
chapters.summary: The first Earth ship enters orbit — not a warship but a transport, carrying the families of the abandoned. The children watch from the school roof, awake, together. Emotional beat: the price paid made visible in what returns.

chapters.title: The Bright Protocol
chapters.summary: Dominic logs the beacon's final entry and re-commissions it under a new protocol of his own authorship: a standing record of what was done, so no one can ever again forget. He signs it with all seven of his names. Emotional beat: memory as the colony's true foundation.
